name: Secondskin — Geneware Pattern Photography Archive
creator: Tomás Bekele-Johansson
description: A photographic archive and exhibition series documenting the full range of cosmetic geneware body modification across all tiers of GLMZ, shot in the tradition of large-format portrait photography with subjects posed in their domestic environments. Bekele-Johansson spent eight years photographing over three thousand individuals, from Tier 1 subjects with DIY geneware modifications done in unlicensed parlors to Tier 5 subjects with bespoke multi-year gene-sculpting programs. The archive is maintained as both physical prints and a neural-feed gallery.
medium: physical large-format photography prints and neural-feed gallery
cultural_impact: Produced the most comprehensive visual document of geneware culture in M88 and fundamentally shifted public perception of DIY modification from deviant to culturally rich; the physical prints are now held in three institutional collections.
controversy: Several Tier 5 subjects have sought to have their portraits removed from the archive, arguing that being placed alongside Tier 1 subjects constitutes reputational harm — a claim that became its own cultural flashpoint about tier hierarchy and shared humanity.
story_hooks: A subject in the archive is now using a completely different genetic profile and claims the portrait proves they were someone they no longer are — and they need that proof to disappear.
One of the Tier 5 subjects attempting to suppress their portrait is hiding something the photograph inadvertently documents in the background of their domestic environment.
Bekele-Johansson left behind an unpublished second archive — photographs he chose not to include — and someone with unclear motives is trying to acquire it.
